mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the Ultimate Parent Company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent Company Registry or Court of the jurisdiction of the parent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the competent apostille authority of the parent jurisdiction if it is a member of the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention; if not a member, Consular Legalization at the Republic of Korea Embassy or Consulate with jurisdiction over the parent jurisdiction. Apostille and Consular Legalization are mutually exclusive and never chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing of the Ultimate Parent Company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate Registry or Tax Authority of the parent jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the issuing jurisdiction's competent authority when the Apostille Convention applies; otherwise Consular Legalization by the Korean diplomatic mission covering that jurisdiction. No sequential combination of Apostille and Consular Legalization is permitted.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney authorizing Korean incorporation and bank account opening
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Ultimate Parent Company Board of Directors
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization by a licensed notary in the issuer's jurisdiction, followed by Hague Apostille if the issuer is in an Apostille member state; otherwise, notarization followed by Consular Legalization at the Korean Embassy or Consulate in that non-member state.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association of the Ultimate Parent Company or Proposed Korean Chusik Hoesa
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Ultimate Parent Company or Founding Shareholders, with notarial certification
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization, then Hague Apostille by the competent authority if the jurisdiction is an Apostille Convention state; for non-member states, notarization followed by Consular Legalization at the Korean diplomatic post in the issuing jurisdiction.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter for Ultimate Parent or Key Shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Financial institution holding an active account for the beneficial owner or parent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank letterhead authentication, plus Hague Apostille if the bank's jurisdiction is an Apostille member; otherwise Consular Legalization by the Korean Embassy or Consulate with territorial competence. No dual-path chaining.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Beneficial Ownership Declaration and Identity Passport Copies of Every Shareholder and Director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Beneficial owners, directors, and a licensed attorney or notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Identity documents attested by a notary, followed by Apostille certification if issued in a member jurisdiction; if the jurisdiction is not an Apostille member, attested documents must undergo Consular Legalization at the Korean Embassy or Consulate.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Prior to onboarding any shareholder, director, AP or ultimate counterparty, we conduct a multi-jurisdictional sanctions and PEP screening against the OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UK HM Treasury Sanctions List, and the Republic of Korea's own designated persons list published by the Financial Services Commission and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Under the Financial Transaction Reports Act (FTRA), we apply a mandatory risk-based approach to identify politically exposed persons, including foreign PEPs, domestic PEPs with senior public functions, and international organization officials, obtain UBO declarations for every natural person controlling 25% or more of the Chusik Hoesa, and verify positive matches through official ID documents, alias checks, and negative news. We also screen the entire corporate family tree for bribery, enforcement actions, and cross-check the business scope against export control lists. The screening is repeated quarterly and upon any ad hoc trigger, and all results are documented for KOFIU inspection.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Korean Court Online Registration System (Internet Registration Office, IRO) administered by the Supreme Court of Korea, accessible via the electronic case management portal at www.iros.go.kr
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A Chusik Hoesa must have a statutory name written in Hangul, ending with the corporate form marker 주식회사 or abbreviated 주. The name must not be identical or deceptively similar to any existing registered corporate name, and must not misrepresent the entity's business or public status. Foreign corporations or individuals may also file a transliterated Hangul trade name based on phonetic transliteration; the four-tier naming convention typically comprises (1) a distinctive brand slogan, (2) the industrial activity descriptor, (3) optional geographic or brand qualifier, and (4) the mandatory corporate form suffix. English-language trade names are permitted for banking, contracts, and external marketing but are not part of the official registry name unless separately registered.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If a name is rejected, the applicant or its legal representative shall, within 7 days of receipt of the rejection, file a written administrative objection with the competent District Court Registry. The objection must state the grounds of appeal, attach a fresh name search report from the IRO system, and provide a legal memorandum demonstrating that the proposed name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered corporate name. The registry must adjudicate the objection within 14 days; if the rejection is sustained, the applicant may either apply for a court order under the Non-Contentious Case Litigation Procedure Act or file a new name reservation without prejudice. No extension of the 30-day reservation window is available, but the applicant may immediately re-file a new reservation with a slightly modified name after withdrawing the original reservation.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Under the Commercial Act and National Tax Service (NTS) enforcement guidance, a virtual office or shared office may qualify as a statutory registered seat if it has a physical mailing address, a lease agreement, and a person available to receive court and tax documents during ordinary business hours. However, a pure commercial mailbox or PO box is categorically rejected by the court registry and NTS. For a vertical micro-drama streaming company with Apple IAP and Google Play payment rails, the main Korean banks typically treat a virtual office as an indicator of low commercial substance and will insist on an in-person site visit, a local director or employee, and evidence of payroll or operational equipment before opening a corporate bank account. Therefore, a virtual office is permissible only if the provider supplies a dedicated suite, a formal lease, signage rights, and a locally employed representative; otherwise, it will trigger enhanced due diligence and may delay bank onboarding.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Risk score: 7/10 within the first 180 days after incorporation due to NTS new-business verification. The mandatory inspection checklist includes: (1) a signed lease or virtual-office agreement covering the exact registered floor and unit; (2) visible signage on the office entrance; (3) a documented payroll or staff presence during business hours; (4) physical evidence of equipment or records; and (5) mail delivery to the registered address with matching utility or telecommunication invoices. An unannounced registry visit is moderate (3/10) and usually triggered by a complaint or inconsistency in the incorporation filing.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, Act No. 1000 of 1962, as amended, particularly Articles 288, 289, 290, 295, 317, 318, 329, 332, 383, 389, 393, 407, 409, and 415 concerning the formation, registration, share subscription, registered office, directors, representative director, and auditors of a Chusik Hoesa (stock corporation).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registration Division of the competent District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office in the Republic of Korea, using the Supreme Court of Korea's Internet Registration System, for example the Registration Division of the Seoul Central District Court for a Seoul registered office.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Chusik Hoesa (stock corporation) together with the notarized Articles of Incorporation, capital deposit certificate, subscribers list, consents of directors and auditor, registered office proof, and registration tax payment receipt.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None under the Commercial Act; no minimum paid-in capital is prescribed for a Chusik Hoesa, and one Korean won per share is permissible. However, the aggregate issue price of all subscribed shares must be deposited into a dedicated capital subscription account in the name of the company-in-formation at a licensed Korean bank, and withdrawals are blocked until the certified certificate of incorporation registration is issued. Registration tax of 0.4% of paid-in capital, a 20% local education surcharge, and court fees are payable, with the estimated minimum state fee being approximately USD 40 for a nominal capital company.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [●] CHUSIK HOESA (THE COMPANY), A STOCK CORPORATION ESTABLISHED UNDER THE COMMERCIAL ACT OF THE REPUBLIC OF KOREA. WHEREAS the Company has been formed by lawful incorporation proceedings, and its shares have been subscribed and deposited in the Company's capital subscription account; and WHEREAS the board is authorized to adopt all resolutions necessary to commence the production and global distribution of vertical micro-dramas and related digital content through mobile streaming applications and third-party payment platforms. NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED: 1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION AND ALLOTMENT. The board ratifies, confirms, and adopts the subscription and allotment of [●] ordinary shares with a par value of KRW [●] per share, issued at an aggregate subscription price of KRW [●], all of which have been fully paid into the Company's blocked capital subscription account or, where applicable, contributed as non-cash property whose valuation has been verified in accordance with the Commercial Act. The representative director is directed to update the register of shareholders, issue share certificates, and maintain the paid-in capital records lawfully. 2. BANKING AND PAYMENT-RAIL AUTHORIZATION. The board authorizes the opening and operation of corporate bank accounts with [●] Bank, including any foreign currency or settlement accounts, and authorizes the representative director, chief financial officer, or their lawful delegates to sign account mandates, execute wire transfers, and establish payment settlement arrangements with Apple IAP, Google Play Billing, and Stripe, subject to the internal financial policy approved by the board. 3. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION. The board adopts [●] as the Company's registered office and legal domicile in the Republic of Korea for all statutory notices, court service, tax correspondence, and corporate records. The representative director is authorized to execute and maintain the lease or sublease for such address and to file the address with the competent registration court and National Tax Service. 4. APPOINTMENT OF STATUTORY OFFICERS. The board appoints [●] as representative director and chief executive officer, [●] as inside director, and [●] as auditor, or, where applicable, as a member of the audit committee, each appointment to take effect immediately and continue until the next general meeting of shareholders or as otherwise provided by the Articles of Incorporation. Each appointee is authorized to act singly or jointly as required by law, to execute contracts, to hire employees, to represent the Company before courts, government agencies, banks, and foreign authorities, and to do all things necessary to carry out the Company's business. 5. GENERAL RATIFICATION AND AUTHORITY. Any actions taken by the incorporators, directors, or officers before this resolution for the purpose of incorporation, capital deposit, lease execution, or preliminary business contracts are hereby ratified, confirmed, and adopted as actions of the Company. The corporate seal and signature arrangements shall be maintained in accordance with the Commercial Act and the internal control policy. This resolution is effective immediately and may be executed in counterparts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-Incorporation Name Search and Articles of Incorporation Drafting
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration System and the competent District Court Registration Division
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct pre-incorporation checks using the Supreme Court of Korea's Internet Registration System to confirm that the proposed Korean and English corporate trade name is not identical to an existing company name in the same jurisdiction and does not contain prohibited words. Prepare the draft Articles of Incorporation with the corporate purpose covering motion picture and video production, vertical micro-drama development, digital content distribution, mobile streaming application services, and ancillary business. The draft must specify the trade name, purpose, total authorized shares, par value, number of shares issued at incorporation, registered office address, notice method, and incorporators. Engage a local filing agent or attorney to verify that each proposed director, representative director, and auditor is qualified and not disqualified under the Commercial Act.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate trade name in Korean and English
Draft Articles of Incorporation
Business plan and detailed corporate purpose statement
Identity documents of incorporators, directors, and auditor
Power of attorney for local filing agent if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is rejected for similarity or misdescription, select up to three alternate names and resubmit the name check. If the registry or drafting attorney identifies a defect in the corporate purpose or share structure, amend the Articles of Incorporation before notarization and perform a new name search if the trade name is changed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Subscription Deposit and Blocked Account Confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Korean commercial bank selected by the incorporators under the Real Name Financial Transactions Act and foreign exchange reporting rules
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the share subscription agreement and cause each incorporator or subscriber to deposit the full issue price of subscribed shares into a dedicated capital subscription account opened in the name of the company-in-formation at a licensed Korean bank. The bank will hold the funds in a blocked status and will not release the deposit until the incorporation registration is completed and the Registration Division issues the corporate certificate. Obtain a deposit certificate from the bank stating the depositor name, company-in-formation name, amount deposited, account number, and blocked release condition. The bank will conduct customer due diligence, verification of ultimate beneficial owners, and source-of-funds screening; all subscribers must provide clean identification documents and cooperate with anti-money laundering inquiries.
required_dossiers: Executed share subscription and allotment agreement
Bank account opening application forms
Proposed Articles of Incorporation
Identity documents and source-of-funds statements for all subscribers
Proof of registered office address such as a lease contract
Foreign investment report confirmation or exemption note if any subscriber is non-resident
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank pauses or rejects the deposit due to a customer due diligence query, promptly submit the requested passport or alien registration card, corporate structure chart, source-of-funds evidence, and a written explanation of the business model. If the bank still refuses, open a new blocked subscription account at another licensed Korean bank and transfer or re-deposit the funds, then obtain a fresh deposit certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korean notary public authorized to authenticate incorporation documents in the jurisdiction of the Company
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the final draft Articles of Incorporation to a Korean notary public for authentication and notarization. The notary public will confirm the identity and legal capacity of each incorporator or their lawfully appointed proxy, verify the existence and consent of the initial directors and auditor, and ensure that the Articles include all mandatory matters prescribed by Article 289 of the Commercial Act. The notary will also confirm that the corporate purpose, share issuance provisions, registered office address, and notice method are lawful and consistent with the deposit certificate. Once notarized, the Articles become the governing charter of the Company and the primary attachment to the incorporation registration application. Any change to the share structure, corporate purpose, or registered office before registration must be made by notarized amendment or by preparing a corrected notarized Articles document.
required_dossiers: Final draft Articles of Incorporation
Capital deposit certificate issued by the bank
Identity documents of all incorporators
Written consents of directors and auditor to their appointments
Name search confirmation printout or equivalent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary public requests clarification or refuses to notarize due to a legal defect, correct the identified provision and resubmit the amended Articles for notarization. If an incorporator cannot appear in person, prepare and notarize a specific power of attorney in the appropriate form, or arrange for the incorporator to appear before a Korean consulate where required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Court Registration of Incorporation and Issuance of Corporate Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registration Division of the competent District Court through the Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration System or in-person filing window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the application for registration of incorporation of the Chusik Hoesa to the Registration Division of the District Court having jurisdiction over the registered office. Attach the notarized Articles of Incorporation, bank certificate of capital deposit, list of subscribers, consents of the directors and auditor, proof of the lawful registered office, and payment receipt for the registration tax and local education surcharge. The Registration Division will examine whether all statutory formation conditions are met, whether the business purpose is lawful, whether capital payment is properly evidenced, and whether the directors and auditor have validly consented. Upon approval, the court enters the Company into the commercial register and issues the certificate of incorporation registration, which is effective as the legal birth of the company and releases the blocked capital deposit.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Capital deposit certificate and confirmation from the bank
Subscribers list and subscription payment records
Written consents and acceptance letters of directors and auditor
Proof of registered office such as lease contract or title certificate
Completed application form for registration of incorporation
Receipt of payment of registration tax and local education surcharge
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registration Division issues a correction order or requests supplementary materials, cure the stated defect within the prescribed statutory grace period by submitting corrected Articles, a revised bank certificate, new consents, or an additional power of attorney. If the defect is substantive and cannot be cured, withdraw the application, amend the Articles, and submit a new application with the corrected documents and additional fees.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Tax Registration, Business Seal, and Corporate Bank Account Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service through HomeTax and the competent local district tax office; the issuing bank for corporate seal certificates
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the certificate of incorporation registration is issued, apply to the National Tax Service for a business registration certificate and value-added tax registration. Present the corporate registration certificate, notarized Articles of Incorporation, representative director's identification, lease contract, and corporate bank account confirmation. After the tax registration is issued, use the corporate certificate and representative director's identification to activate the previously blocked capital subscription account as a regular corporate business account, and obtain a corporate seal certificate if desired. For the vertical micro-drama streaming application business, complete the technical and compliance onboarding required by Apple IAP, Google Play Billing, and Stripe by providing the corporate certificate, business registration certificate, bank account details, tax clearance letter or equivalent, and a board resolution identifying the settlement account and authorized signatories.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation registration
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Business registration application form
Corporate lease contract and electricity or utility bill for office address
Representative director's passport or alien registration card
Confirmation of corporate bank account details
Deposit certificate or final block-release confirmation from the bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office rejects the business registration due to an incomplete office address or lease documentation, provide a corrected lease agreement, a utility bill in the corporate name, or a landlord's certificate of occupation and resubmit. If the bank requires additional anti-money laundering information for account activation, provide an updated corporate structure chart, source of funds, expected transaction volume, and authentication of the beneficial owner, then reapply for the bank clearance.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable; this scope involves digital content production and global distribution of vertical micro-dramas and is not a physical manufacturing, chemical processing, assembly, or warehousing operation under ISIC 5911.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable for industrial Civil Defense fire permits, Environmental Impact Assessment, or occupational licensing; the company is a digital content production and streaming distribution enterprise. General workplace safety obligations under the Occupational Safety and Health Act and ordinary office fire safety compliance, if any employees are engaged, remain the responsibility of the registered employer.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: The National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea, administered electronically through the HomeTax portal at www.hometax.go.kr; import and export clearance is handled by the Korea Customs Service (KCS) through the UNI-PASS electronic clearance system at unipass.customs.go.kr.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: register the Chusik Hoesa with the Korean Commercial Court registry upon incorporation. Step 2: within 20 days of business commencement, file the business registration application with the NTS district office that has jurisdiction over the registered head office, using the HomeTax portal; attach the Articles of Incorporation, certified registry excerpt, lease agreement or title proof for the registered address, and the representative director's identification. Step 3: receive the Business Registration Certificate carrying the 10-digit Business Registration Number, which is the unified corporate TIN and VAT ID. For a foreign non-resident entity with no domestic place of business that supplies taxable services or digital content in Korea, the entity must appoint a Korean tax representative and file the HomeTax foreigner registration application with a power of attorney, the foreign certificate of incorporation, the tax representative's identity details, and a statement of expected Korean-source revenue; the NTS then issues a dedicated VAT registration number for indirect tax and withholding compliance. No invoice may be issued and no input VAT deduction may be claimed until the registration is approved.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Korean tax law has no US-style check-the-box or entity-classification election. The elections relevant to a Chusik Hoesa are: (i) the consolidated corporate tax return election for a wholly owned domestic group under the Corporate Tax Act; (ii) the elective hybrid-mismatch self-adjustment mechanisms under the International Tax Adjustment Act for reverse hybrid, double-deduction, or deduction-without-inclusion arrangements; and (iii) the annual choice between foreign tax credit and treaty exemption. No election can convert the Chusik Hoesa into a pass-through or territorial-only taxpayer.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act of the Republic of Korea
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No monetary threshold exists before mandatory VAT registration; every person supplying taxable goods or services in Korea must register. The only small-business accommodation is the simplified taxpayer regime, which requires annual turnover below KRW 80 million and applies to small sole proprietors only. A Chusik Hoesa is always a general taxpayer and is subject to full VAT registration, invoicing, and return obligations regardless of turnover.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Korea mandates an electronic tax invoice for every B2B supply. The supplier must issue the e-tax invoice through an NTS-certified e-invoicing provider or the HomeTax EDI/API and transmit it to the NTS by the day following issuance. Every e-tax invoice carries an accredited digital certificate signature; an invalid signature renders the invoice ineffective for input VAT deduction. For B2C digital supply, the platform must issue and report cash receipts in real time through the NTS cash-receipt system. Anti-fraud enforcement relies on real-time cross-matching of issued e-tax invoices against VAT returns, customs export declarations, foreign-exchange receipts, and app-store payout data. Korea does not operate a Latin-American style fiscal stamping clearance, but the electronic signature and next-day filing obligations function as the equivalent digital clearance mandate.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero rating is available under Article 21 of the Value-Added Tax Act for (i) goods exported and cleared by the Korea Customs Service; (ii) services supplied to non-residents or foreign corporations when the place of supply is outside Korea; and (iii) digital content services, including vertical micro-drama streaming, monetized through Apple IAP, Google Play Billing, or Stripe for overseas end users, provided the actual viewing or exploitation occurs outside Korea and consideration is received in foreign currency. The Korean supplier must prove the foreign place of supply through contract terms, platform payout reports, and geolocation or device metadata; if the proof is absent, the revenue is reclassified as domestic taxable supply at 10% VAT.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Korea Customs Service Export Declaration and Export Clearance Receipt, together with the Bill of Lading or Air Waybill for physical shipments.
Signed international service, licensing, and streaming-distribution agreement with the foreign counterparty defining the licensed territory and remuneration basis.

App-platform settlement and payout statements from Apple App Store Connect, Google Play Console, and Stripe, supported by commercial invoices and subscriber/geolocation logs showing foreign end users.
Inward Remittance Certificate or Foreign Exchange Earned Certificate issued by an authorized foreign exchange bank in Korea evidencing the repatriation and conversion of the export proceeds.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The NTS reconciles every zero-rated export invoice against the customs export declaration, the underlying contract, the platform payout statements, and the foreign-exchange inward remittance. For digital services, NTS auditors may also inspect IP geolocation logs, device metadata, and app-store country reports. If foreign-currency proceeds are not received within 180 days of the export date (or service performance date) without an approved NTS extension, or if the documentation bundle is incomplete, the zero rating is revoked retroactively and the supply is assessed at 10% VAT. The assessment is increased by underreporting penalties of 10% for simple error, 20% for gross negligence, 30% for intentional underreporting, and 40% for fraudulent false invoices under the Framework Act on National Taxes, plus a daily late-payment interest charge currently set at approximately 0.022% per day. Knowingly creating false export declarations or zero-rating evidence triggers criminal liability under the Punishment of Tax Evasion Act, carrying imprisonment or monetary fines up to 3 to 5 times the tax evaded. The ordinary statutory assessment period is 5 years, 7 years where no return was filed, and 10 years for fraudulent evasion. Genuine zero-rated exporters can claim refunds of excess input VAT through the semi-annual VAT return, but the refund is held until the same documentation bundle passes the NTS pre-refund review.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) as central bank, together with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act (FETA); authorized Korean foreign exchange banks perform delegated control and reporting.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea operates a market-determined managed float for the Korean won. Current account transactions, including trade, royalties, content licensing, subscriptions, dividends and interest, are broadly liberalized and require no prior permission, although a resident corporation must retain underlying contracts and the bank must report the transaction to the foreign exchange information system. Capital account transactions are also significantly open, but Korean won remains primarily convertible through onshore authorized foreign exchange banks and offshore non-deliverable trading is an offshore market not available to the Korean resident entity. Inward direct investment into a Chusik Hoesa is routed under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act: the foreign investor files a pre-investment report, remits equity funds into a foreign-currency undertaking account in a domestic bank, and provides a certificate of capital payment for registration of the foreign-invested enterprise. Profit remittance in the form of dividends is treated as a current transaction and can flow out after corporate tax clearance, withholding tax payment, distributable-reserve verification, and board approval; there is no blanket dividend lock, but the bank will require the balance sheet, audit report where statutory, and tax certificate plus a foreign exchange bank report. The Korean won is not an international settlement currency outside formal banking rails, and certain non-resident won account transfers remain subject to reporting. Overall, Korea is a high-convertibility but high-documentation jurisdiction rather than a hard surrender-currency regime.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory mandatory conversion ratio exists in South Korea; a resident exporter may retain 100% of export proceeds in a foreign currency account at an authorized foreign exchange bank and decide the timing of conversion to Korean won. Export proceeds must be collected in accordance with FETA timelines, generally within 90 days of shipment or performance date unless an extension is approved by the dealing bank; overdue collection is reported to the bank and BOK/MOEF through the reporting system. The synthetic surrender requirement is effectively zero under the liberalized current-account framework, and conversion, when elected, is effected at the spot market rate.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Foreign Investment Enterprise Capital Escrow Account and Basic Korean Won Operational Account
Foreign Investment Proceeds Deposit Account and Basic Korean Won Operational Account
FIPA-Designated Foreign Currency Subscription Account and Domestic Settlement Account
Corporate Operational Currency Account with Foreign Exchange and Trade Settlement Clearing

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Very low as a primary treasury banking solution. Offshore digital EMI platforms are not banks under the Korean Banking Act and cannot legally provide a domestic KRW checking account with access to the Korea Financial Telecommunications and Clearings Institute rails. A foreign EMI without an FSC license under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act is restricted from performing money transmission in Korea, and even a licensed electronic money provider is not a substitute for a Chusik Hoesa corporate bank account because it cannot complete FIPA capital registration, hold foreign currency deposit accounts, issue foreign exchange certificates, verify inbound direct investment, or process corporate tax payments. EMIs may be used only as a supplementary collection tool for limited non-KRW customer payments, not as the cross-border liquidity clearing rail. The only compliant route for the Stage 4 treasury function is a domestic tier-1 bank or licensed domestic branch of a foreign bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is the default. At least one registered statutory director of the Chusik Hoesa, normally the representative director or a locally domiciled signatory possessing the corporate seal certificate, must appear in a Korean bank branch during account opening for identity confirmation and specimen seal signature. Remote videoconference opening is occasionally available for domestic directors using an accredited K-Cert digital certificate, but for foreign shareholders and directors the standard practice is in-branch verification. Alternatively, a non-resident director may grant a notarized power of attorney apostilled at a Korean consulate or Korean notary office where applicable, and the appointed attorney must appear physically. Tele-presence or remote consular proxy opening is not universal and is strictly subject to bank-specific e-KYC and anti-money-laundering policy approval.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity around the Chusik Hoesa capital structure, particularly the risk of nominee shareholders or layered ownership among foreign investors.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Corporate register and complete organizational chart, current shareholder ledger with all share transfers, passports and tax identification numbers for every natural person holding 10% or more, a UBO declaration identifying each individual owning more than 25%, source-of-wealth statements for the equity injection, notarized ownership self-certification confirming no nominee arrangements, and apostilled corporate records where required.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inward FDI capital may arrive in fragmented low-value wires from third-party accounts or a related-party treasury center, creating ambiguity between equity capital and shareholder loans.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed equity subscription agreement and board resolutions, pre-investment foreign investment report under FIPA, remittance instructions showing transfer from the investor's own bank account, 12 months of bank statements for the remitting investor, certificate of incorporation of the foreign investor, sanctions and PEP screening results, legal counsel certification that funds are not derived from criminal proceeds, and a reconciliation of every inward wire against declared capital.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Vertical micro-drama revenue flows arrive through Apple IAP, Google Play Billing and Stripe rather than traditional trade invoices, making expected turnover difficult to reconcile with FX flows and corporate tax filings.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed platform agreements with Apple and Google, Stripe merchant settlement reports, monthly payout statements from app stores, the short-drama content licensing and intellectual property ledger for all titles, user subscription and conversion analytics, intercompany license agreements with related content owners, and OECD transfer pricing documentation if royalties are paid to a foreign parent.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Royalty and distribution counterparties may be located in higher-risk jurisdictions or connected to adverse media and PEP profiles, triggering enhanced due diligence before treasury onboarding.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full KYB on each distribution licensee and strategic partner, sanctions and adverse media screening reports dated within 30 days from a recognized commercial database, PEP attestation forms for every beneficial owner, bank reference letters for material counterparties, distribution agreements with commercial substance, delivery and performance records, and a written business-rationale notice explaining the geographic counterparty selection.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The foreign investor must remit equity subscription funds from the investor's own bank account to the Chusik Hoesa's foreign investment undertaking account at an authorized Korean foreign exchange bank. A SWIFT MT103 order message should include in field 70 the FIPA declaration or registration number, the company identifier KR_CHUSIKHOESA, and the label FDI_EQUITY_SUBSCRIPTION as accepted by the dealing bank. The receiving bank credits the foreign currency deposit account, certifies receipt of the foreign direct investment capital, and carries out the post-investment foreign-invested enterprise registration via the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy/KOTRA and MOEF/BOK reporting channels. The KRW conversion is executed as a spot FX trade at the prevailing market rate. Capital verification is completed by an independent accountant using the bank-issued foreign currency receipt certificate, the share subscription agreement, and the board resolution approving issuance of shares. All underlying corporate documents must be retained for the bank's foreign exchange audit and capital verification file.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For operating expenses, local production costs, cloud hosting, contractor payments and content marketing, the treasury desk should instruct SWIFT MT103 from the Korean won or foreign currency operational account through the bank's online corporate treasury portal, retaining invoices, contracts and tax receipts. For physical imports of equipment or documentary purchases, use a commercial letter of credit issued via MT700 and documentary collections where appropriate. For outgoing royalties or license fees to the overseas parent, execute MT103 with the withholding tax payment receipt, signed royalty agreement, corporate tax clearance certificate, and transfer pricing documentation. Current-account payments are free of prior approval but require reporting and evidential record-keeping; the bank is responsible for filing foreign exchange reports and will impose an annual period for retaining transaction documents. All trade settlements must be supported by customs declarations where the underlying involves cross-border movement of goods.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable onshore KRW/USD forward contracts with a Korean licensed bank, limited to the amount and tenor of confirmed underlying export, import, royalty, subscription or dividend exposure.

Cross-currency swaps and FX swaps matching foreign currency borrowings and interest payment schedules, provided the underlying borrowing is registered with the foreign exchange bank and the swap transaction is hedging-only.

Foreign currency options and option-based strategies with a premium or zero-cost collar structure designed to hedge expected app-store revenue and distribution receivables, permitted only after the underlying exposure is evidenced by signed contracts and financial forecasts.

Offshore non-deliverable forwards NDFs are not permissible for the Korean resident Chusik Hoesa; hedging must be executed onshore in deliverable Korean won. Non-resident counterparties may access the offshore NDF market separately, but the Korean entity cannot use those instruments as its treasury hedge.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporation Income Tax Return for the fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the fiscal year-end; for a December 31 fiscal year-end, the deadline is March 31. A one-month extension to April 30 is available when the return is prepared or transmitted by an accredited certified tax accountant or certified public accountant.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing imposes an additional tax equal to 20 percent of the reported tax due (40 percent for fraudulent or intentionally evasive returns), plus late-payment interest of 0.022 percent per day from the original due date. Continued non-payment and non-filing expose the company to compulsory collection, seizure of bank accounts and receivables, revocation or forced closure of the business registration, and court-led dissolution or administrative strike-off where no legitimate business activity is proven.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting approval of financial statements and consolidated annual records
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Meeting of Shareholders; minutes and supporting records retained at the registered office in Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The annual shareholders meeting must be convened within 3 months after the end of the fiscal year; for a December 31 fiscal year-end, the final statutory meeting date is March 31.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: There is no filing fee, but officers who fail without just cause to convene the annual meeting or who submit false minutes are subject to administrative fines under the Korean Commercial Act, typically not exceeding KRW 10,000,000. The failure also creates audit and tax documentation failures that can lead to the National Tax Service disregarding internal book records and imposing formal use of the representative-specific estimated assessment.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: First-half Value-Added Tax return and payment for the January through June period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due by July 25 immediately following the end of the first VAT period. For foreign-sourced digital drama revenue, the return must still be filed with supporting zero-rated export documentation where applicable.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing of the VAT return triggers an additional tax equal to 10 percent of the unpaid VAT liability, or 0.5 percent of the tax amount for unfaithful returns, plus late-payment interest of 0.022 percent per day. Repeated delinquency can result in forced closure of the registered business place, seizure of accounts, and revocation of the business registration by the National Tax Service.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Second-half Value-Added Tax return and payment for the July through December period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due by January 25 following the end of the fiscal year; for a December 31 fiscal year-end, the return is due January 25 of the next calendar year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The same VAT delinquency regime applies: an additional tax equal to 10 percent of unpaid VAT, late-payment interest of 0.022 percent per day, compulsory seizure, business place closure, deregistration, and potential criminal referral for willful failure or concealment.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, a private Chusik Hoesa is statutorily required to appoint an independent certified public accountant for an external audit when the company is listed on a Korean exchange, when it is a public-interest entity under the Enforcement Decree, or when its total assets at the immediately preceding fiscal year-end equal or exceed KRW 12,000,000,000. Balance-sheet, turnover, and headcount triggers are not set as standalone audit thresholds for an unlisted micro-drama entity below that asset level, but a voluntary audit is required contractually by many venture investors, international streaming licensors, and cross-border payment intermediaries; if the company owns an overseas subsidiary, consolidated K-IFRS audited financial statements may also be required for parent-level or banking purposes.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korea International Financial Reporting Standards are mandatory for listed companies and public-interest entities; private Chusik Hoesa entities may apply Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles, including the SME Accounting Standards issued under the Korean Accounting Standards Board, unless the entity is part of a consolidated group required to use K-IFRS. Revenue from vertical micro-drama streaming, Apple IAP, Google Play billing, and Stripe settlement is recognized under K-IFRS 1115 / IFRS 15 as performance obligations satisfied over time, with net revenue presentation only where the company acts as principal under the relevant digital store agreement.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: South Korea does not impose a separate annual UBO confirmation return for a private Chusik Hoesa incorporated under the Commercial Act. Beneficial ownership is verified at the transactional level through financial institution KYC/CDD obligations. However, under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, a non-resident beneficial owner who holds 10 percent or more of the shares or a qualifying value-based stake must report the acquisition to the competent foreign-exchange bank and register the foreign investment; subsequent changes in foreign ownership, transfers, or additional contributions must be reported to the Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency and the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy within 30 days. Domestically, all share transfers must be entered in the company register of members without delay, and the transfer is not opposable to the company until the register is updated; the corporate income tax return must separately disclose major shareholders with a 10 percent or more equity interest and any related-party transactions.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Charges and Mortgages if applicable
Minute Book of General Meetings and Board of Directors
Register of Bondholders if debt instruments are issued

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,000 - USD 3,500 per year for a Seoul- or Jeju-based registered office and local compliance agent; law-firm registered agent services inclusive of statutory mail processing are typically USD 1,500 - USD 3,000 per year.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,000 - USD 15,000 for a full Korean-IFRS or K-GAAP statutory audit of a micro-drama holding and streaming distribution entity with simple capital structure; a review-level compilation for a company below the mandatory audit threshold is typically USD 2,500 - USD 5,500.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% headline marginal rate on taxable income exceeding KRW 300 billion, with a progressive structure of 10% on taxable income up to KRW 200 million, 20% above KRW 200 million up to KRW 20 billion, 22% above KRW 20 billion up to KRW 300 billion, and 25% above KRW 300 billion
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory tax holidays are not generally available to domestic Chusik Hoesa. Applicable incentives include R&D expense tax credits, facility investment tax credits, Free Economic Zone and Foreign Investment Zone incentives for eligible foreign-invested high-technology businesses, job-creation credits for start-ups and venture companies, and special tax support for innovative growth industries. A separate patent-box regime does not exist in Korea; IP-derived income is taxed at ordinary corporate income tax rates.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Base and Tax Calculation Return (법인세 과세표준 및 세액계산서 신고서) with supplementary non-resident withholding schedules, filed electronically through the National Tax Service HomeTax System at www.hometax.go.kr
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual on a fiscal-year basis. Quarterly interim prepayments are required for a resident Chusik Hoesa; a foreign corporation with a Korean permanent establishment is also subject to interim prepayment obligations.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within three months from the end of the fiscal year. A fiscal year ending 31 December has a statutory filing deadline of 31 March of the following year. An extension does not extend the tax payment deadline; penalties accrue from the day after the original payment due date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable corporate income computed from the audited financial statements after tax adjustments, including loss carryforwards and transfer-pricing adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a Korean-incorporated Chusik Hoesa wholly owned by non-residents, the same taxable income schedule applies. All foreign-source revenue must be separated from Korean-source revenue, and the company cannot make a non-resident election. Payments to a non-resident parent for management or IP services are deductible only if commercially reasonable, properly documented, and subject to transfer-pricing analysis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statutory adjustments covering non-deductible contributions, excess officer compensation, excessive entertainment expenses, thin-capitalization interest disallowance, and other book-to-tax differences.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Intercompany charges paid to a non-resident shareholder or foreign affiliate for royalties, app-store fees, content licensing, and management services must be supported by contracts, invoices, and economic substance evidence. If the recipient is a non-resident without a Korean PE, gross-basis withholding tax of 20% plus 2% local surcharge must be reflected. Excessive charges are recharacterized as non-deductible disguised dividends.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 - Foreign Tax Credit and Foreign-Source Income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credit for foreign income taxes paid on overseas royalty receipts and international distribution revenue of the vertical micro-drama application.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Chusik Hoesa must attach the Foreign Tax Credit Schedule and provide a tax residency certificate from the source country to substantiate the foreign tax credit. Double relief is denied where a reciprocal recovery is obtained through a mutual agreement procedure; the recovered amount is treated as taxable dividend income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 - Withholding Tax Schedule on Non-Resident Payments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report of dividends, interest, royalties, rents, outsourcing fees, and technical service fees paid to non-resident shareholders, lenders, and licensors.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the gross amount paid to each non-resident recipient, the statutory withholding rate of 20% corporate income tax plus 2% local income tax surcharge, and the applicable treaty rate code. The treaty rate can be applied only when the company holds the beneficiary's Tax Residency Certificate, beneficial ownership declaration, and ownership period evidence before the filing deadline; otherwise the full 22% must be withheld and remitted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 - Minimum Tax and Special Incentive Computation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Application of the 15% alternative minimum corporate income tax on adjusted taxable income and preferential statutory deductions for qualifying industries or employment increases.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a capital-light digital content company, the 15% minimum corporate tax may apply when statutory credits and deductions reduce the effective rate below 15%. No non-resident exemption exists for the minimum tax, and the calculation excludes the effect of any non-resident shareholder-level benefit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 - Resident Corporation Declaration and PE Status
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of whether the filing entity is a resident Korean corporation or a foreign corporation with a domestic business establishment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a Korean-incorporated Chusik Hoesa, the resident corporation box must be selected. Non-resident investors are not identified in this schedule. A foreign parent that has no Korean PE does not file a Korean corporate tax return for Korean-source passive income such as dividends, interest, or royalties because such income is subject to final withholding tax.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing or non-filing triggers an unfaithful-return penalty of 10% or 20% of the unpaid tax, or 40% if the omission is fraudulent. Interest is charged at 0.022% per day from the due date until payment. Failure to attach required schedules incurs fixed penalties under the Framework Act on National Taxes, and criminal referral is available under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act when the omitted tax is large or the filing is deceptive, with imprisonment up to 2 years for basic evasion and up to 5 years for aggravated amounts.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% corporate income tax withholding on gross dividends paid to a non-resident corporate shareholder, plus a 2% local income tax surcharge equal to 10% of the corporate income tax withheld, yielding an aggregate statutory rate of 22%. Under an applicable Double Tax Treaty the dividend withholding rate may be reduced to 5%-15%, generally conditioned on the beneficial owner holding a minimum equity stake of 10%-25% for 365 continuous days.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief, the non-resident shareholder must (1) obtain a Tax Residency Certificate issued by the contracting state tax authority within the previous 12 months, (2) complete the National Tax Service application for non-resident tax exemption or reduction, (3) provide a beneficial ownership declaration and an ownership history schedule proving the required holding period, and (4) deliver the documents to the Korean withholding agent before the payment date. The Chusik Hoesa submits the dossier through HomeTax with its monthly withholding tax return. If the reduced treaty rate is applied without complete documentation, the National Tax Service will retroactively assess the 22% statutory rate with penalties and interest. Refunds of excess withholding are processed through the ordinary national tax refund procedure, which normally takes 60-90 days after a complete application.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding on cross-border royalties and interest is 20% corporate income tax plus 2% local surcharge, totaling 22%. Most Korean Double Tax Treaties reduce interest to 10%-15% and royalties to 5%-10%, subject to beneficial ownership and the absence of a Korean permanent establishment that effectively connects the income. For vertical micro-drama distribution royalties paid to a foreign production house, the withholding obligation attaches when the payment is deductible by the Korean resident corporation or the liability is sourced to a Korean business.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Under the Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs and its Enforcement Decree, a Korean corporation with international related-party transactions exceeding KRW 5 billion in the prior fiscal year must prepare and retain a Local File and file the related-party transaction report. A Master File is required when the consolidated worldwide group revenue exceeds KRW 100 billion. The National Tax Service may request contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation below these thresholds during an audit, so a prudent threshold for internal preparation is KRW 1 billion in cross-border related-party transactions.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea does not operate a formal Economic Substance Regulations regime comparable to the UAE ESR. Economic substance is enforced through the substance-over-form principle under the Corporate Income Tax Law, thin-capitalization rules, controlled foreign corporation rules, and treaty anti-abuse doctrine. A Korean Chusik Hoesa operating a vertical micro-drama app must perform core income-generating activities through resident employees: content commissioning, IP licensing, platform pricing, server administration, user acquisition, and marketing. If all decision-making and risk-taking occurs outside Korea and the Korean entity is only a cash conduit, profits may be reattributed to the beneficial owner and the entity treated as a shell.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion and fraudulent understatement of digital-content revenue
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Reporting only a portion of global in-app subscription revenue generated through Apple IAP, Google Play Billing, or Stripe while the residual profit is shifted to a foreign affiliate through a sham commission agreement or an undisclosed offshore payment pipeline, with the purpose of evading progressive Korean corporate income tax and non-resident dividend withholding.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty under Framework Act on National Taxes Articles 47-3 and 47-4: 20% of the unpaid tax for an unfaithful return and 40% for a dishonest fraudulent return. Under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act Article 3, the corporation may be fined up to 10 times the evaded tax and the responsible officer may be sentenced to imprisonment of up to 2 years, escalating to 5 years when the evaded amount exceeds KRW 300 million or the falsification is especially serious.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director may lose limited liability through judicial piercing of the corporate veil if the company is found to be an alter ego or a shell. The National Tax Service may hold the director jointly and severally liable for unpaid corporate taxes, interest, and penalties. Personal asset seizure, an overseas travel ban, and exit-hold orders are available when unpaid tax exceeds KRW 100 million, and criminal conviction can result in imprisonment and disqualification from corporate management.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to withhold and remit statutory withholding tax on non-resident payments
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends, royalties, or interest to a non-resident parent or offshore IP-holder without deducting the 20% corporate income tax and 2% local surcharge, or applying a treaty-reduced rate without a current Tax Residency Certificate, beneficial ownership declaration, and ownership holding-period documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The withholding agent is liable for the unpaid withholding amount plus an underreporting penalty under Framework Act on National Taxes Article 47-2. The National Tax Service can assess the full 22% statutory rate retroactively, deny treaty relief, and impose an additional daily interest charge. Where the payment is a disguised dividend, the recipient and the Korean entity face a corporate tax adjustment on the profit distribution.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The representative director and senior financial officer are jointly and severally liable when the company fails to withhold or remit and the director participated in the payment decision. Willful failure to remit withheld taxes can be prosecuted as embezzlement or breach of trust under the Criminal Act, carrying imprisonment of up to 3 years and a fine up to KRW 50 million. Directors who sign false withholding filings also face criminal tax fraud charges and personal restitution orders.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company abuse and sham core income-generating activities
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the Korean Chusik Hoesa with no employees, no board meetings, no IP ownership, no cash-flow autonomy, and no real risk-bearing, while entering back-to-back content licensing and management contracts that strip the Korean margin to a zero-tax or low-tax foreign affiliate, all for the purpose of avoiding Korean corporate tax and dividend withholding.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The National Tax Service may disregard the sham contracts under the substance-over-form rule in Article 14 of the Corporate Income Tax Law, recharacterize purportedly deductible fees as non-deductible distributions, and assess the full 22% withholding on the recharacterized dividends. The adjustment is subject to 20% or 40% penalty rates depending on culpability. Treaty benefits are denied, and the Korean entity may be sanctioned as a shell with revoked business registration and a criminal referral for tax evasion.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly implement or benefit from the shell structure are stripped of the limited-liability shield. They are jointly and severally liable for the avoided taxes, penalties, and interest, may face criminal prosecution with imprisonment of up to 5 years, and may suffer an international travel ban, asset forfeiture, and personal bankruptcy risk if the corporation is found to be the alter ego of a non-resident director or beneficial owner.
